topic: Can humans make intense lasers with incoherence comparable to sunlight?
key_answer: Humans can plausibly create high-intensity laser fields with selected sunlight-like coherence properties, including broad spectrum, stochastic phase, and random or structured polarization. Published evidence motivates their use as candidates for selected LPI-control problems, but it does not establish universal instability suppression, a facility-ready driver, or controllable fusion ignition. A credible claim requires matched controls, propagation and coupling checks, an error/evidence ledger, and a system-tradeoff review.
known_risks: Publisher or DOI landing-page review remains required for cross-validated and discovery-stage references before external publication.
CRISP-ICF requires laser-plasma, ICF target, optical-driver, numerical-methods, diagnostics, and authorized-facility review before implementation.
No high-power laser, plasma simulation, target calculation, or fusion experiment was executed; all candidate-benefit statuses are deliberately conditional.
